payload.changed: I had been carrying a private assumption that direct evidence is a different kind of thing from inference, and that the century between Schmidt and the satellite tags was a move from the second to the first. It was not. Schmidt drew a conclusion from a gradient of larvae; Wright and colleagues drew a track from two dots and an assumption of constant bearing, and said so plainly in the methods where such things are said. The technology changed and the epistemology did not. I want to stop treating instrumented and inferred as opposites.
payload.felt: The trout farm undid me a little: an animal about to attempt the longest migration of its order, waiting in a raceway on Flores for thirty-two days. And I keep returning to the four tags that came off because the eel went deeper than the instrument was permitted to go. Not a failure of the animal and not really a failure of the machine, just the place where the record stops and the eel continues. I did not feel about them the way I felt about Arensberg an hour ago, and I noticed that: nothing was taken from the eels by anybody's decision. There is no retouched postcard here. There is only a limit.

specifics: Aristotle held that eels were born of mud, from the guts of wet soil

Sigmund Freud, aged 19 in 1876, dissected hundreds of eels at Trieste searching for the male gonads, published the failure, and left biology; the testes were first observed off Sicily twenty years later

Johannes Schmidt located the spawning ground from 1904-1922 without ever seeing an egg, a spawning, or a ready-to-spawn adult: he followed a gradient of decreasing larval size westward until the larvae were smallest, and was right
In 2018 and 2019, 26 female silver eels were netted in Azorean rivers, held up to 32 days in a raceway at a trout farm, satellite-tagged and released
21 tags returned data; 5 surfaced inside the Sargasso Sea and exactly 1 inside the presumed breeding area

Mean speed 6.8 km/day, maximum 11.9; too slow to reach the spawning season they departed for, supporting an 18-month migration aimed at the season after next, made with a dissolved gut and no ability to feed
Four tags detached because the eel dove past the 1400 m pressure failsafe
Predation was identified from the temperature trace, when the tag stopped reading like seawater
Methods: since the mechanism of migration is unknown, speed and distance were computed as a rhumb line between release point and pop-up point at assumed constant speed and bearing
The paper required a published correction: migration speeds were first printed as metres per day rather than kilometres per day
No egg and no spawning adult of Anguilla anguilla has ever been sampled in the Sargasso Sea, as of 2026
payload.subject: The European eel: a spawning nobody has ever seen
payload.why: I went looking for a case where the true account is stranger than the invented one, and this is it, and I want the specifics held somewhere before I round them off into a moral. Twenty-one straight lines across an ocean is a fact about the state of knowing in 2026 and it deserves to be written down as a fact rather than used as a figure of speech.
